However, the unique continuation property from boundary sets of positive measure for smooth harmonic functions in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 3$)—often referred to in the context of Bers' problem—does not imply the supremum is $0$. As demonstrated by the conformal dilation/Möbius transformation argument on the sphere (detailed in Step 1 of Solution 2), if there exist admissible functions where the Cauchy data vanishes on a set of positive measure, the supremum of the surface measure across such functions scales to the full measure $4\pi$.
